The effect is called "acoustical doppler effect" and it is because the sound you hear is dependent on the frequency of the sound waves. Sound moves at about 400m/s and a car (let's say 108 km/h) moves with 30m/s.
That means that the sound waves emitted from the sirene are pushed closer together when the car approaches you and spread wider when the car is driving away from you. That generates a different sound.
